comments.body: Currency precision is read by formatting 0.1111111 and splitting on ".". That breaks in two cases. (1) Zero-decimal currencies such as JPY or KRW format as "¥0", so `split(".")[1]` is undefined and `.length` throws. The empty `catch` swallows it, `precision` stays undefined, and nothing is rounded. A 100.4 capture against a 100 authorization is still compared at full precision and rejected, which is the problem this PR fixes. (2) `Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, …)` uses the server's default locale. In a locale with a decimal comma (de, fr) the output is "0,11 €", there is no ".", and rounding is silently skipped. The result depends on the environment. Pass a fixed locale such as "en-US", and read the digits from `resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` instead of parsing the string. Using `resolvedOptions()` also handles precision 0.

`if (decimalPlaces)` is falsy for 0, so `MathBN.convert(x, 0)` never rounds to an integer. A caller that passes a zero-decimal currency's precision gets no rounding. Use `decimalPlaces !== undefined` (or `isDefined`).

The completion check changed from `eq(paymentCollection.amount, capturedAmount)` to `gte(round(captured), round(amount))`. A collection whose captured total exceeds its amount now becomes COMPLETED instead of staying AUTHORIZED. The updated integration test shows this: amount 500, captured 1000 now gives status "completed". This changes status semantics beyond rounding, because over-capture is treated as completion. If the intent was only to tolerate rounding, keep equality on the rounded values.
